title: Sample-Specific Output Constraints for Neural Networks
verified_locator: Printed p.6816, Supported Constraints and Generalizations, final bullet; guard phi(z,s)=exp(z)+b. Method fig.1 and Eqs.(3)-(4).
source_mechanism: Differentiable sample-dependent output guard; constraint descriptor also enters learned network.
source_target: Facial landmark regression and vehicle follow-object control.
current_E3_overlap: A positive learned excess added to a sample-specific lower bound.
current_E3_difference: E3 uses b=sqrt(A)+1e-4*a_tr and a_tr*softplus(z), with A derived from six observed returns. It does not implement the full arbitrary-constraint architecture.
R1_consequence: The broad floor-plus-positive-excess mechanism is already explicit. The particular bound and softplus substitution do not establish a substantive adaptation by themselves.
limits: No exact E3 target or training recipe identified here. This conceptual antecedent does not prove historical copying or universal nonnovelty.

title: Lipschitz Normalization for Self-Attention Layers with Application to Graph Neural Networks
verified_locator: §3.3 Eq.(2), PDF p.3; §5 Eqs.(17)-(18), PDF p.5; sentence after Eq.(17) states Q is a model parameter.
source_mechanism: Softmax pooling with linear query scores and LipschitzNorm score normalization.
source_target: Graph neural network and graph Transformer tasks.
current_E3_overlap: Softmax pooling and a learned query independent of the input at inference.
current_E3_difference: E3 bounds parameters and latent states but does not implement the LipschitzNorm denominator of Eq.(17).
R1_consequence: A learned query and weighted attention pooling are not sufficient novelty claims. A genuinely modified propagation rule would need its own comparison.
limits: The graph depth instability is not established as a defect of the shallow E3 encoder.

title: The Lipschitz Constant of Self-Attention
verified_locator: §3 Theorem 3.1; §6 Conclusion and Discussion, PDF p.8, paragraph beginning the bounded-input alternative.
source_mechanism: Non-Lipschitz standard dot-product attention on unbounded domains; Lipschitz L2 attention; discussion of compact inputs.
source_target: Attention analysis and character-level language modelling.
current_E3_overlap: Analysis of attention regularity under an explicitly bounded latent domain.
current_E3_difference: E3 proves a conditional bound for its scalar head with fixed parameters and fixed floor, not the paper’s L2 attention or a bound from raw OHLCV.
R1_consequence: Having a bound on a compact latent domain is technical evidence, not by itself a new mechanism or raw-input robustness guarantee.
limits: No transfer of the L2-attention theorem to E3. All hypothesis domains must remain explicit.

title: HARNet: A Convolutional Neural Network for Realized Volatility Forecasting
source_mechanism: Causal dilated convolutions initialized to reproduce a HAR baseline; loss-specific optimization analysis.
current_E3_overlap: Neural volatility forecasting with explicit domain structure and causal filters.
current_E3_difference: E3 uses a short centered-return volatility target and an additive output guard; it does not use the HAR initialization or filters.
R1_consequence: Causal convolution and incorporating financial structure into a network are established. A new adaptation must specify what beyond that is changed.
limits: RV, sigma7 and their loss functions are different estimands; reported errors are not directly comparable.

title: Probabilistic Forecasting Cryptocurrencies Volatility: From Point to Quantile Forecasts
source_mechanism: QRS residual simulation, quantile linear regression and quantile regression forests over point forecasts.
source_target: Next-day daily BTC realized variance from 288 intraday five-minute returns; 99 conditional quantiles.
current_E3_overlap: Probabilistic uncertainty for crypto volatility; baseline LSTM and MLP are included.
current_E3_difference: E3 is a point model of centered rolling seven-return sigma, with a deterministic sample-dependent floor. The paper’s quantiles are a separate meta-forecasting layer.
R1_consequence: Adding quantiles or probabilistic forecasts in crypto is not by itself new; a future law-based head needs a much narrower algorithmic distinction.
limits: Preprint v1; no exact finite-atom U-to-sigma pushforward mechanism is identified in the examined sections. That absence is bounded, not global.

authors: Yang, Lorch, Graule, Lakkaraju and Doshi-Velez
title: Incorporating Interpretable Output Constraints in Bayesian Neural Networks
verified_locator: §4 Definitions 4.1–4.3, Eqs.(1)–(2); §4.1 conditional output-constrained priors; §4.2 approximate inference.
source_mechanism: Deterministic/probabilistic output constraints induced through Bayesian output-constrained priors.
source_target: Low-dimensional simulations, clinical action, recidivism and credit prediction.
current_E3_overlap: Input-dependent admissible output sets and constraints on predictive distributions.
current_E3_difference: E3 uses an architectural point-output guard with a deterministic lower bound; it has no weight posterior or COCP inference.
R1_consequence: Output-support knowledge and probabilistic output constraints are established; the broad phrase support-aware probabilistic network cannot sustain novelty alone.
limits: Soft approximate posterior constraint satisfaction is not equated with E3’s architectural hard inequality. A proposed new head must specify its distinct rule.
